grades.quote: When two or more threads operate on a shared data structure, some very strange malfunctions can occur if the timing of the threads turns out precisely so that they interfere with one another.
grades.reason: Introduces races on shared data: threads whose timing interferes cause malfunctions. Its example updates a shared count (seatsRemaining = seatsRemaining - 1), which is analogous to a shared counter increment. The excerpt stops before it walks through the lost-update interleaving, so it explains the general cause but not the full mechanism.
Covers proportional-share scheduling (CFS weights and time slices). It says nothing about shared counters or lost updates from races.
Scheduling exploration exercises about processor time and FIFO priority scheduling. It is unrelated to the shared-counter race.
